headline: High: shared filesystem and broad write/network defaults create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks between Cline and Flowise.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files and use MCP; Flowise can read/write server filesystem and ingest uploaded files. That creates a plausible shared-file bridge where content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. This is not provably blocked, but it is not a direct default parser hijack either.
conditions: IF Cline writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace file and Flowise later ingests that file as flow input, injection is possible.
IF Flowise exposes uploaded content back into a workspace that Cline parses as instructions, the bridge becomes bidirectional.
mitigations: Use separate directories for Cline and Flowise workspaces.
Disable file-based handoff between the two agents.
Require manual review of any file passed from one agent to the other.
Restrict Flowise uploads to a quarantine folder.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and has broad network egress; Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs plus uploaded files and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace or datastore, sensitive code or uploaded content can flow into either agent’s outputs or outbound API calls in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or server datastore, file contents can leak across the pair.
IF Flowise routes uploaded files to model providers or HTTP tools, those contents can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Separate secrets and source code into different folders.
Turn off uploads in Flowise unless needed.
Use local-only model providers for both agents.
Review outbound tool calls before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files, and Cline can modify git state while Flowise can write server filesystem. In a shared directory or repo, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state. The profiles show no locking or coordination primitive, so the conflict is plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF Cline and Flowise operate on the same repository or directory, concurrent writes can race.
IF Flowise stores generated artifacts in a git-tracked path, Cline may commit stale or conflicting state.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Pause one agent before the other writes to shared files.
Avoid git operations while Flowise is active.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based orchestration layer that can treat upstream outputs as tool inputs, while Cline can generate code, browser-derived facts, and file edits. If Flowise consumes Cline’s output without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or tool calls. No built-in verification is shown in either profile.
conditions: IF Flowise uses Cline-generated text as an action input without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF Flowise nodes trigger external tools based on Cline output, the cascade can become operationally harmful.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents.
Require schema validation on all Cline outputs before Flowise consumes them.
Limit Flowise to read-only actions until outputs are checked.
Log and diff intermediate artifacts.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles browser screenshots and source code, while Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and uploaded files. Their docs-only profiles do not specify retention, residency, or deletion controls, so a shared deployment can easily create mismatched handling of the same data class. Uncertainty pushes this above low because compliance gaps are not ruled out.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents, retention or residency mismatches may occur.
IF one deployment logs uploads longer than the other, deletion requests may be only partially honored.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair.
Document retention settings for both systems.
Disable verbose logging where possible.
Confirm residency for each backend provider.
requires-engineering: align deletion and export workflows.
